feed.title: NPR Topics: Politics
feed.subtitle: Follow NPR Politics for nonpartisan coverage of government, elections, policy debates and voting rights. Plus weekday audio from The NPR Politics Podcast.

entry.title: Chris Van Hollen says he will challenge Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader
entry.summary: Van Hollen, a progressive from Maryland, said voters sent a clear message in the midterm elections — that they want "change from the status quo."

entry.title: Cindy Holscher wins in Kansas, holding governor's office for Democrats
entry.summary: Holscher, a state senator, overcame a more well-known Republican who had Trump's endorsement in the state that has gone to the GOP in most other statewide races.

entry.title: Democrats want to stop Trump's arch, golf course and more. What are their options?
entry.summary: As Trump's arch and other projects make their way through the courts, many critics are looking to Congress to stop them. Democrats have a few tools, including funding and oversight.

entry.title: Witnesses describe the D.C. shooting that left 1 dead, 4 injured
entry.summary: A gunman opened fire at a gym in Washington, D.C.'s Logan Circle Thursday morning. One person has been confirmed killed and four others injured. The gunman is dead, according to police.

entry.title: Colom wins Mississippi Senate race. And, White House warns Dems over future probes
entry.summary: After more than a week of counting ballots, Scott Colom has narrowly won the Mississippi Senate seat. And, the White House has sent a letter warning Democrats who plan to investigate the administration.

entry.title: Senators don't always share bill text online before votes. They should, advocates say
entry.summary: The text of what lawmakers are considering isn't always made available for public review before it is voted on. A group of open governance advocates is calling on Senate leadership for a change.

entry.title: A blue wave helped offset for now a falling tally of Black members in the U.S. House
entry.summary: A Supreme Court ruling that further weakened the Voting Rights Act paved the way for a record drop in Black representation in Congress. But a midterm blue wave helped hold off such a decline for now.

entry.title: At least 23 states considered laws governing ICE and schools this year
entry.summary: When ICE agents show up at a school, educators rely on a patchwork of policies to know what to do. This year, many state legislatures tried to update those policies.

entry.title: How Scott Colom defied the odds to go from DA to Mississippi's Democratic U.S. senator
entry.summary: In a state that hasn't had a Democrat in office since 1980 and hasn't sent a Black senator to Washington since the 1870s, Colom's win represents a massive upset in state politics.
